questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think it is important to meet other people from other countries. This makes your academic view of your fields of study broader. Furthermore, I think it is important to see how another university works. This makes you a better student.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a really nice experience. I met a lot of amazing people and really got a lot of new academic knowledge.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was nice. Everthing worked great with Erasmus and both Copenhagen and maastricht university provided the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got an email and then there was a meeting for all the exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was really good

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing. My best advice is to start very early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live off campus, but close to campus and where all the other students are located.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing and the available housing was old and expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really easy. They have a really nice Exchange Officer for Incoming Students. His name is Silvester Conduto.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just choose a course and then it gets approved, if you did the registration within the time limit.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was easy to get help. Silvester Conduto answered emails very fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100%. I got all the courses, which I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the course, which you like the must. Look at the courses beforehand, so you can register in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had interesting and very international/european course, which is nice, because you get more useful knowledge.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was difficult, but not too difficult. you had to study, but not a lot. It was reasonable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very diffrent, because Maastricht University use PBL. It worked good and is properly the best way to learn, if the teacher is willing to help the students, but is was something you should get used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UM sports is a great way for students to meet each other and do sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of bars and cafes in maastricht. Furthermor, there is a lot of diffrent associations at the university - e.g. a running club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to UM sports, it is really nice, if you want to do sport and meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore the rest of europe. Maastricht is in the heart of europe. Germany, france and Belgium is only mor for less than an hour away from maastricht by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, because The Netherlands and Denmark are similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to the diffrent activities and try to talk with people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not any big differences to be honest.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate how nice people are to each other in The Netherlands. it is really a trust based country with sweet people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find accommodation in good time 
Prepare your English, because you will need to talk a lot in Class
Get an ESN arrival ticket in the beginning, because that is the best way to meet people in the start 
Sign up for UM sports, because you will do sports and meet people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a university with a lot of students from all over europe, that is nice, because everyone speaks English, which is very nice for meeting new people. The university can be a bit much, because the academic level is high, so be prepared.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be social and to do good in the courses, because that is a difficult balance, but, in my opinion, you have to do both, for an exchange to be nice

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Im really glad for my exchange. It was a great stay.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
